submissions.title: County Council unanimously approves 18-month data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: Montgomery County Council voted unanimously to approve an 18-month data center moratorium; no new permits can be issued during that period.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Montgomery County, MD Council passed an 18-month moratorium in a final unanimous vote on Jul 28 2026, barring new data center permits countywide. Builds on County Executive Elrich's June 2026 executive order that already halted the permitting department from accepting/processing data center applications. No currently tracked project sits in Montgomery County, MD, so this isn't linked to a project row — flag for siting-restriction linkage if one is added later.

submissions.title: Nvidia weighs $250 billion guarantee so OpenAI can lease SoftBank's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus
submissions.excerpt: Nvidia weighs $250 billion guarantee so OpenAI can lease SoftBank's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus
submissions.suggestedProjectName: PORTS Technology Campus (Piketon, Pike County, Ohio)
submissions.note: SUGGESTED NEW PROJECT — not currently tracked (distinct from tracked 'Stargate Lordstown', which is in NE Ohio; this site is in Pike County, southern Ohio). SB Energy/SoftBank is building a 10 GW data center plus ~10 GW of on-site gas generation at the former DOE Portsmouth uranium-enrichment site. DOE/Commerce partnership announced Mar 20 2026, with SB Energy citing $33B for the power plant plus $4.2B for AEP Ohio grid upgrades (site-power basis, not IT load; project gained federal FAST-41 permitting status Jun 16 2026 at a cited $67.2B total). Fresh news (WSJ, reported ~Jul 27 2026): Nvidia is reportedly negotiating a roughly $250B financing guarantee so OpenAI can lease the campus as a Stargate site, which could push all-in cost including chips past $500B. Terms are unsettled and the deal could still collapse — treat as reported/unconfirmed, not a done deal. Likely the same 'Midwest' site referenced in OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank's prior five-new-Stargate-sites announcement.

claims.methodology: 10 GW data center target stated by DOE/SB Energy at the Mar 2026 groundbreaking; site power/generation basis, not yet built or energized

SB Energy-stated initial investment ($33B power plant + $4.2B AEP Ohio grid upgrades) per the DOE/Commerce partnership announcement; excludes the separately reported $250B Nvidia financing guarantee and chip costs

submissions.title: SK Group and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership Across AI Factories and Next-Generation Memory
submissions.excerpt: SK Telecom is building a 2-gigawatt NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory in Korea to serve global compute demand.
submissions.suggestedProjectName: SK Telecom Vera Rubin AI Factory (Korea)
submissions.note: SUGGESTED NEW PROJECT, distinct from the tracked 'SK Telecom–AWS Ulsan AI Data Center.' Announced Jul 24 2026 as part of a $500B+ SK Group–Nvidia letter of intent spanning AI factories and next-gen HBM4 memory (with SK hynix). SK Telecom will build a 2 GW AI factory — described by SK as the largest in Korea — on Nvidia's Vera Rubin DSX platform, built in phases starting 2027. Exact site/location was not disclosed in the announcement or follow-on coverage (left blank on purpose); it may turn out to be a new phase of the Ulsan site or a wholly separate location — flag for reviewer to confirm before merging into Ulsan or creating a new row. No capex figure disclosed for this specific facility (the $500B+ figure spans the whole SK–Nvidia partnership, not this one site).

claims.methodology: Stated directly by NVIDIA/SK Group joint announcement: '2-gigawatt NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory'
